[...] But in 1885 another fire destroyed over a hundred of the paintings in storage in a wing of the museum.

gancho: Desde cerca de 256 a.C., um sistema de irrigação na China controla as cheias do rio Min sem represá-lo: um dique em forma de boca de peixe divide a água e manda mais para as lavouras na seca e menos na cheia.
explicacao: O rio Min descia das montanhas cheio do degelo da primavera, perdia velocidade na planície de Chengdu, acumulava sedimento e transbordava. Li Bing, hidrólogo do Estado de Qin, podia ter feito uma barragem, mas Qin queria manter o rio aberto para os barcos militares que abasteciam as tropas na fronteira. A solução foi desviar parte do fluxo com um dique feito de cestos compridos de bambu trançado cheios de pedras. O dique "boca de peixe" separa um braço interno, fundo e estreito, de um braço externo, raso e largo. Na estação seca, o braço interno leva cerca de 60% da água para a irrigação; na cheia, a fatia cai para 40%, e o braço externo leva embora boa parte do sedimento. Faltava abrir um canal na montanha, numa época anterior à pólvora. Li Bing aquecia a rocha com fogo e a esfriava com água até ela rachar, e depois de oito anos havia um corte de 20 metros de largura. Degradado nas convulsões do século XVII e destruído por um terremoto em 1933, o sistema foi reconstruído e ainda irriga mais de 5.300 km². Desde 2000, é Patrimônio Mundial da Unesco.

fontes.trecho: Originally constructed around 256 BC by the State of Qin as an irrigation and flood control project, it is still in use today. [...] Originally, the Min would rush down from the Min Mountains and slow down abruptly after reaching the Chengdu Plain, filling the watercourse with silt, thus making the nearby areas extremely prone to floods. King Zhao of Qin commissioned the project, and the construction of the Dujiangyan harnessed the river using a new method of channeling and dividing the water rather than simply damming it. The water management scheme is still in use today to irrigate over 5,300 km2 (2,000 sq mi) of land in the region [...] Dujiangyan Irrigation System was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2000. [...] Qin hydrologist Li Bing investigated the problem and discovered that the river was swelled by fast flowing spring melt-water from the local mountains that burst the banks when it reached the slow moving and heavily silted stretch below. One solution would have been to build a dam, but the Qin wanted to keep the waterway open for military vessels to supply troops on the frontier, so instead an artificial levee was constructed to redirect a portion of the river's flow [...] The levee was constructed from long sausage-shaped baskets of woven bamboo filled with stones known as Zhulong [...] Cutting the channel proved to be a far greater problem, as the hand tools available at the time, prior to the invention of gunpowder, would have taken decades to cut through the mountain. Li Bing devised an ingenious method of using fire and water to rapidly heat and cool the rocks, causing them to crack and allowing them to be easily removed. After eight years of work, a channel 20 meters (66 ft) wide had been gouged through the mountain. [...] The original Dujiangyan irrigation system was destroyed by the 1933 Diexi earthquake. The current Dujiangyan irrigation system was rebuilt after the Diexi earthquake in 1933 [...] It is an artificial levee that divides the water into inner and outer streams. The inner stream is deep and narrow, while the outer stream is relatively shallow but wide. This special structure ensures that the inner stream carries approximately 60% of the river's flow into the irrigation system during dry season. While during flood, this amount decreases to 40% to protect the people from flooding. The outer stream drains away the rest, flushing out much of the silt and sediment. [...] Turmoil surrounding the conquering of Chengdu by peasant rebel leader Zhang Xianzhong in 1644, and the Ming-Qing transition more generally, led to depopulation and the deterioration of the Dujiangyan irrigation system to the point where rice cultivation was set back for decades.

gancho: O maior túmulo do Japão, um monte de cerca de 500 metros, é atribuído ao imperador Nintoku, mas não há como confirmar: ele fica sob a guarda da Casa Imperial, que restringe o acesso até de arqueólogos.
explicacao: Entre meados do século III e o início do século VIII, o Japão ergueu cerca de 160 mil kofun, montes de terra e pedra sobre túmulos da elite. Os maiores têm formato de buraco de fechadura. O de Daisen, em Sakai, perto de Osaka, é o maior do país: cercado por três fossos, teria levado uns 20 anos para ser construído, em meados do século V, e estima-se que o monte tenha sido coberto por cerca de 50 milhões de pedras. Boa parte das atribuições de túmulos a imperadores vem do século XIX. Depois da restauração do poder imperial, em 1868, o governo atribuiu muitos túmulos a personagens das crônicas Kojiki e Nihon Shoki, do início do século VIII, e, como o imperador era tido como divino, eles ganharam caráter sagrado. Depois da derrota de 1945, os cerca de 900 túmulos atribuídos a ancestrais imperiais passaram à Agência da Casa Imperial como túmulos privados, e o acesso continuou proibido, decisão cercada de polêmica. Ficam perguntas sem resposta: quem está enterrado ali? Os túmulos teriam provas de uma ascendência coreana da família imperial? Mesmo com sinais oficiais recentes de abertura, quase ninguém de fora da agência consegue entrar. O monte está tomado pela vegetação, e os fossos viraram refúgio de peixes e aves aquáticas.

fontes.trecho: The Daisenryo Kofun (大仙陵古墳, Daisenryō kofun), the largest kofun in Japan, is believed to have been constructed over a period of 20 years in the mid 5th century during the Kofun Period.  While it cannot be accurately confirmed, it is commonly accepted that the tomb was built for the late Emperor Nintoku. The Imperial Household Agency of Japan treats it as such. [...] In the Japanese archipelago, more than 20,000 tumuli (kofun), which are mounds of earth and stones erected over graves of the ruling class, were built between the later part of the 3rd century and the 6th century. [...] The larger ones are keyhole-shaped (zempō kōenfun) [...] The Daisen Kofun mound is approximately 500 metres (1,600 ft) long and 300 metres (980 ft) across at its widest point, while the entire tomb area is 840 metres (2,760 ft) long. Enclosed by three moats [...] Today, the tomb is off-limits and protected by the Imperial Household Agency in the centre of Sakai City.  The moats have been maintained and provide a sanctuary for fish and waterbirds.  The mound itself is completely overgrown by vegetation.

fontes.titulo: Japan's royal tombs: Burial mounds and Korean connections in the 3rd-8th centuries AD (Current World Archaeology, 2024)
fontes.trecho: following the restoration of imperial power in 1868, the Japanese government assigned many tombs to personages mentioned in ancient chronicles, specifically the Kojiki ('Records of Ancient Matters') dating to 712 and the Nihon Shoki ('Chronicles of Japan') drawn up in 720. As the emperor was regarded as divine, these tombs took on special sacred significance. Following Japan's defeat in 1945, and the Showa Emperor's renunciation of his divinity, the 900 or so tombs attributed to imperial ancestors came into the guardianship of the Imperial Household Agency as private graves. Access to them continued to be forbidden, a decision around which controversy has swirled. Many questions remain, such as who was buried within? Do the tombs contain proof that the Japanese imperial family was in fact of Korean descent? [...] Despite recent official statements suggesting some change in policy, access continues to be largely denied to anyone beyond the Imperial Household Agency. [...] It is estimated that some 160,000 burial mounds (kofun in Japanese, meaning ‘old mound’) were constructed between the middle of the 3rd century AD and the early 8th century.

fontes.titulo: Archaeologists Investigate Japan's Daisen Kofun (Archaeology, 27 nov. 2018)
fontes.trecho: is thought to have been built in the mid-fifth century A.D. for Emperor Nintoku. Little is known about the structure, however, because in the past access to it has been limited by Japan's Imperial Household Agency. Scholars think the mound itself was covered with some 50 million stones.

gancho: Em 1986, operários na China acharam covas com milhares de objetos de ouro, bronze e jade, quebrados, queimados e enterrados com cuidado. A cultura que os fez tinha um estilo desconhecido e não deixou registros escritos.
explicacao: O sítio de Sanxingdui, na província de Sichuan, tem peças datadas por radiocarbono dos séculos XII e XI a.C. Elas são da mesma época da dinastia Shang, mas num estilo de bronze bem diferente, e os pesquisadores se espantaram com uma arte totalmente desconhecida na história chinesa. Há dezenas de grandes máscaras e cabeças de bronze com olhos amendoados exagerados, algumas com as pupilas saltadas para fora, e orelhas enormes. Há também a estátua humana de pé, em tamanho natural, mais antiga do mundo, com 260 centímetros, e uma árvore de bronze de 396 centímetros, com pássaros e flores. As peças foram quebradas, talvez de propósito, num ritual, depois queimadas e enterradas. Há pistas: crônicas compiladas mais de mil anos depois dizem que o fundador do reino de Shu, Cancong, tinha olhos saltados, como as máscaras, mas há outras interpretações. Sem registros escritos, é difícil saber para que serviam os objetos, e o fim dessa cultura também é debatido: desastres naturais, com sinais de grandes enchentes e de um terremoto, ou a invasão de outro povo. Seis novas covas, escavadas entre 2020 e 2022, renderam mais peças, entre elas uma máscara de ouro.

fontes.trecho: Largely discovered in 1986, following a preliminary finding in 1927, archaeologists excavated artifacts that radiocarbon dating placed in the 12th–11th centuries BC. [...] According to the Chronicles of Huayang that were compiled during the Jin dynasty (266–420), the Shu kingdom was founded by Cancong (蠶叢). Cancong was described as having protruding eyes, a feature that is found in many of the masks and figures of Sanxingdui. It has therefore been suggested that the large masks with protruding eyes are a representation of Cancong, although there are other interpretations. [...] In 1986, local workers accidentally found sacrificial pits containing thousands of gold, bronze, jade, and pottery artifacts that had been broken (perhaps ritually disfigured), burned, and carefully buried. [...] Researchers  were astonished to find an artistic style that was completely unknown in the history of Chinese art. [...] The six pits were discovered at the Sanxingdui site between 2020 and 2022 during a renewed slate of excavations. The artifacts found in these excavations include fragments of a gold mask [...] This culture is contemporaneous with the Shang dynasty, but it developed a different artistic style of bronze-making from the Shang. [...] Speculation regarding the end of the Sanxingdui culture includes that it might have been the result of natural disasters (evidence of massive flooding and an earthquake were found), or invasion by another culture. [...] such as the world's oldest life-sized standing human statue (260 centimetres [100 in] high, 180 kilograms (400 lb)), and a bronze tree with birds, flowers, and ornaments (396 centimetres [156 in]) [...] The most striking finds were dozens of large bronze masks and heads (at least six heads with gold foil masks originally attached) represented with angular human features, exaggerated almond-shaped eyes, some with protruding pupils, and large upper ears. [...] As no written records remain it is difficult to determine the intended uses of objects found.

gancho: Livros de sucesso dizem que a rebelião de An Lushan, na China do século VIII, matou 36 milhões de pessoas. O número sai de dois censos, e muitos historiadores acham que ele mede sobretudo o colapso do próprio censo.
explicacao: A rebelião, uma guerra civil contra a dinastia Tang, durou de 755 a 763, chegou a tomar a capital, Chang'an, e despovoou regiões com fome, fugas e destruição. O último censo antes dela, de 755, registrou 52.919.309 pessoas. O de 764, logo depois do fim da guerra, registrou só 16,9 milhões. A diferença, uns 36 milhões, dois terços da população do império, entrou no livro "The Better Angels of Our Nature", de Steven Pinker, como a maior atrocidade da história em proporção, um sexto da população mundial da época, embora o próprio Pinker dissesse que o número era controverso. Matthew White, de quem Pinker tirou a estimativa, depois a revisou para 13 milhões. Historiadores como Charles Patrick Fitzgerald lembram que a guerra foi travada, com interrupções, em três ou quatro províncias. Para eles, os registros do pós-guerra refletem também a perda de precisão do sistema, a retirada da contagem de grupos que não pagavam imposto, como religiosos, estrangeiros e mercadores, e o fato de que províncias do norte, com cerca de um quarto da população, deixaram de prestar contas ao fisco. Em 1947, Hans Bielenstein escreveu que só uma crença "comicamente ingênua" na sede de sangue dos combatentes levaria a ler aquela queda como mortes.

fontes.trecho: The An Lushan rebellion was a civil war in China that lasted from 755 to 763, at the approximate midpoint of the Tang dynasty (618–907). [...] The rebels succeeded in capturing the imperial capital Chang'an [...] the military activities and associated casualties caused significant depopulation from famine, displacement, and large-scale infrastructure destruction [...] the last census undertaken before the rebellion, in 755, recording a population of 52,919,309 in 8,914,709 taxpaying households. However, a census taken in 764, the year following the end of the rebellion, recorded only 16,900,000 in 2,900,000 households. [...] The difference in the census figures amounts to 36 million people fewer, two-thirds of the population of the empire, though scholars have attributed this to factors including a breakdown in taxation and census gathering. The figure of 36 million was used in Steven Pinker's book The Better Angels of Our Nature, where it is presented as proportionally the largest atrocity in history with the loss of a sixth of the world's population at that time, though Pinker stated that the figure was controversial. Matthew White, from whom Pinker had taken the figure of 36 million, later revised his figure down to 13 million [...] Historians such as Charles Patrick Fitzgerald argue that claims of massive depopulation are incompatible with contemporary accounts of the war, which was fought intermittently over three or four provinces. They point out that the numbers recorded on the postwar registers reflect not only population loss, but also a breakdown of accuracy of the census system as well as the removal from the census figures of various classes of untaxed persons, such as those in religious orders, foreigners and merchants. In addition, several of the northern provinces, with approximately a quarter of the empire's population, were no longer subject to the imperial revenue system. [...] In 1947, Hans Bielenstein likewise criticized the conclusions drawn by earlier scholars from rebellion-era censuses, stating: "One must have a comically naive belief in the fighting parties' bestiality and bloodthirst to assert that An Lu-shan's rebellion in 755 should have reduced the population of China from 51.6 million people to 17 million."

gancho: Os guardiões musculosos e furiosos nos portões de templos budistas do Japão teriam um ancestral grego: Héracles. Na arte greco-budista, o herói virou o protetor do Buda, e essa imagem viajou pelo Leste Asiático.
explicacao: O protetor em questão é Vajrapani, nome sânscrito que significa "com o raio (ou o diamante) na mão". Quando o budismo se espalhou pela Ásia Central e se misturou a influências helenísticas, no chamado greco-budismo, o herói grego Héracles foi adotado para representá-lo: um atleta musculoso e peludo, com uma clava curta. Na arte de Gandhara, durante o Império Kushan, Vajrapani aparece sobretudo como protetor de Sakyamuni, o Buda histórico. Há autores que veem nessas imagens não Héracles, mas Zeus, cujo atributo clássico é justamente o raio. De todo modo, a figura de Vajrapani como um lutador forte acabou influenciando as estátuas de divindades guardiãs no Leste Asiático. No Japão, onde ele se chama Shukongōshin, sua imagem inspirou os Niō, os "Reis Benevolentes", os guardiões de expressão feroz e músculos saltados que ficam na entrada de muitos templos budistas. Na China e em Taiwan, formas de Vajrapani também vigiam os portões de templos e mosteiros.

fontes.trecho: As Buddhism expanded in Central Asia and fused with Hellenistic influences into Greco-Buddhism, the Greek hero Heracles was adopted to represent Vajrapāni. In that era, he was typically depicted as a hairy, muscular athlete, wielding a short "diamond" club. [...] Some authors believe that the deity depicted is actually Zeus, whose Classical attribute is the thunderbolt. The image of Vajrapani as a wrestler-like figure would eventually influence the statues of guardian deities in East Asia. [...] During the Kushan Empire, Gandhara art depicted Vajrapani's images in which he is shown primarily as a protector of Sakyamuni and not in the role of a bodhisattva. [...] Manifestations of Vajrapāni can also be found in many Buddhist temples in China, Taiwan and Japan as Dharma protectors guarding monastery and temple gates. [...] In Japan, Vajrapāni is called Shukongōshin (執金剛神), the on'yomi reading of his Chinese name. As in China, his image was the inspiration for the Niō (仁王; Benevolent Kings), the wrath-filled and muscular guardian of the Buddha, found at the entrance of many Buddhist temples. [...] Vajrapāni, "holder of the thunderbolt", is a compound word in Sanskrit in which 'Vajra' means "Diamond or Thunderbolt", and 'pāni' literally means "in hand".

gancho: Em 781, na capital da China Tang, cristãos da Igreja do Oriente ergueram uma estela em chinês e siríaco sobre 150 anos de cristianismo no país. Enterrada em 845, voltou à luz no século XVII, e Voltaire duvidou dela.
explicacao: Segundo a estela, o missionário Alopen chegou em 635, vindo de Daqin, nome chinês para o Império Romano do Oriente, com livros sagrados e imagens, e a Igreja do Oriente foi reconhecida pelo imperador Taizong. O texto, com cerca de 1.900 caracteres chineses e glosas em siríaco, chama Deus de "Verdadeiro Senhor", menciona o Gênesis, a cruz e o batismo e lista uns setenta monges e sacerdotes, alguns com nomes persas. Um deles, Yisi, foi comandante militar na repressão à rebelião de An Lushan, e a corte Tang recompensou a ele e à igreja com títulos e cargos. A pedra foi provavelmente enterrada em 845, durante a perseguição Huichang, voltada ao budismo, mas que também atingiu os cristãos. Desenterrada no fim da dinastia Ming, ela foi traduzida por jesuítas e virou notícia na Europa, onde críticos anticatólicos e antijesuítas disseram que a pedra era falsa ou que os jesuítas tinham mexido no texto. A ideia foi retomada por jansenistas franceses e por Voltaire. Em 1907, o aventureiro dinamarquês Frits Holm foi a Xi'an disposto a levar a estela para a Europa. As autoridades locais o impediram e a transferiram para o museu Floresta de Estelas, onde ela está até hoje. Holm se contentou com uma cópia exata, que mandou para Nova York.

fontes.trecho: is a stele, erected in 781 during the Tang dynasty, that documents approximately 150 years of early Christianity in China. It is a limestone block 279 centimetres (9 ft 2 in) high with text in both Chinese and Syriac describing the existence of Christian communities in several cities in northern China. It reveals that the initial Church of the East had met recognition by the Tang Emperor Taizong, due to efforts of the Christian missionary Alopen in 635. According to the stele, Alopen and his fellow Syriac missionaries came to China from Daqin (the Eastern Roman Empire) in the ninth year of Emperor Taizong (635), bringing sacred books and images. [...] Buried in 845, probably during the Huichang persecution of Buddhism, the stele was not rediscovered until 1625. [...] The stele is thought to have been buried in 845, during the Huichang persecution, which also affected Christians. The stele was unearthed in the late Ming dynasty (between 1621 and 1625) beside Chongren Temple (崇仁寺) outside of Xi'an. [...] The names of several higher clergy (one bishop, two chorepiscopi and two archdeacons) and around seventy monks or priests are listed. [...] Some of the Church of the East monks had distinctive Persian names (such as Isadsafas, Gushnasap), suggesting that they might have come from Fars or elsewhere in Persia [...] Below this headpiece is a long Chinese inscription, consisting of around 1,900 Chinese characters, sometimes glossed in Syriac (several sentences amounting to about 50 Syriac words). Referring to God using the title 真主, Pinyin: Zhēnzhǔ (literally "Veritable Majesty" or "True Lord"), the text refers to Genesis, the cross, and baptism. [...] Yazedbuzid (Yisi in Chinese) helped the Tang dynasty general Guo Ziyi militarily crush the Sogdian-Turk led An Lushan rebellion, with Yisi personally acting as a military commander and Yisi and the Church of the East were rewarded by the Tang dynasty with titles and positions as described in the Xi'an Stele. [...] The Xi'an Stele attracted the attention of some anti-Christian, Protestant anti-Catholic, or Catholic anti-Jesuit groups in the 17th century, who argued that the stone was a fake or that the inscriptions had been modified by the Jesuits who served in the Ming Court. [...] Later, Navarrete's point of view was taken up by French Jansenists and Voltaire. [...] The Danish scholar and adventurer Frits Holm came to Xi'an in 1907 planning to take the monument for himself to Europe. Local authorities prevented him and moved the stele, complete with its tortoise, from its location near Chongren Temple to Xi'an's Beilin Museum (Forest of Steles Museum). Holm had an exact copy of the stele made for him and had the replica stele shipped to New York [...] The original Xi'an Stele remains in the Forest of Steles.

gancho: Num estudo publicado em 2024, uma cidade maia com pirâmides e quadra de jogo de bola apareceu em dados de laser coletados para monitorar uma floresta. Ficava junto à única rodovia da região, e a ciência não sabia dela.
explicacao: O lidar dispara pulsos de laser de um avião e monta um modelo 3D do terreno, mesmo sob mata fechada. Em 2013, um projeto de monitoramento florestal no México, voltado a reduzir emissões do desmatamento, fez um levantamento desse tipo em Campeche e deixou os dados livres. Pesquisadores da Universidade Tulane, liderados pelo doutorando Luke Auld-Thomas, reexaminaram cerca de 122 km² desse material com olhos de arqueólogo. Acharam mais de 6.500 estruturas pré-hispânicas e uma grande cidade desconhecida, que batizaram de Valeriana, por causa de uma lagoa vizinha. Ela tem todas as marcas de uma capital maia clássica: praças fechadas ligadas por uma calçada larga, templos-pirâmide, quadra de jogo de bola e um reservatório feito ao represar um riacho sazonal. Segundo Auld-Thomas, ficava junto à única rodovia da área, perto de uma cidade onde se planta entre as ruínas há anos, e nem o governo nem os cientistas sabiam dela. Como os dados não foram coletados com perguntas arqueológicas em mente, funcionam quase como uma amostra ao acaso. Isso pesa num debate: os mapas feitos em torno de sítios famosos, como Tikal, exageravam a densidade maia? Para os autores, não: cidades e povoamento denso eram comuns em grandes áreas das terras baixas maias centrais.

fontes.titulo: Running out of empty space: environmental lidar and the crowded ancient landscape of Campeche, Mexico (Antiquity, 2024)
fontes.trecho: Published online by Cambridge University Press: 29 October 2024 [...] Here, we present an archaeological analysis of approximately 122km2 of high-quality airborne lidar data collected in 2013 as part of a forest monitoring project called Alianza M-REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation in Mexico) [...] made freely available by Alianza M-REDD+ [...] these expedient datasets have the advantage of being effectively random with regards to the archaeological record; as the data were collected without regard for archaeological questions [...] Block 2 directly overlies the epicentre of a major urban area that was previously unknown to the scientific community. This city, which we call Valeriana (Figures 3, 4 & 5) after an adjacent freshwater lagoon [...] The larger of Valeriana's two monumental precincts has all the hallmarks of a Classic Maya political capital: multiple enclosed plazas connected by a broad causeway; temple pyramids; a ballcourt; a reservoir formed by damming an arroyo (a seasonal watercourse) [...] we can only conclude that cities and dense settlement are simply ubiquitous across large swaths of the central Maya Lowlands.

fontes.titulo: Have we found all the major Maya cities? Not even close, new research suggests (Tulane University via ScienceDaily)
fontes.trecho: was led by Tulane University anthropology doctoral student Luke Auld-Thomas and his advisor, Professor Marcello A. Canuto. [...] Their findings included evidence of more than 6,500 pre-Hispanic structures, including a previously unknown large city complete with iconic stone pyramids. [...] Lidar technology uses laser pulses to measure distances and create three-dimensional models of specific areas. [...] We also found a large city with pyramids right next to the area's only highway, near a town where people have been actively farming among the ruins for years. The government never knew about it; the scientific community never knew about it. [...] The counterargument was that lidar surveys were still too tethered to known, large sites, such as Tikal, and therefore had developed a distorted image of the Maya lowlands.

gancho: Sem roda, o Império Inca mandava recados por corredores em revezamento, com postos a poucos quilômetros uns dos outros. Segundo um cronista, o imperador recebia em Cusco peixe do mar ainda vivo, vindo de 350 a 400 km.
explicacao: A rede de estradas inca, o Qhapaq Ñan, somava dezenas de milhares de quilômetros (uma estimativa comum fala em 40.000 km) e era percorrida a pé: a roda não era usada para transporte. Ao longo dela havia postos chamados chaskiwasi, a cerca de 2,5 km uns dos outros, segundo vários cronistas (outros relatos e estudos modernos falam em distâncias diferentes), onde jovens mensageiros, os chasquis, vigiavam a estrada à espera do próximo colega. Ao avistar o posto, o corredor que chegava gritava e soprava uma trombeta de concha para alertar o substituto. Depois repetia o recado mais de uma vez, até o outro entender perfeitamente, e o novo corredor partia descansado. Os chasquis levavam mensagens faladas, pequenos pacotes e quipus, cordões com nós que registravam sobretudo números, como impostos ou soldados a deslocar; não há prova de que soubessem lê-los. Estima-se que o sistema levasse um recado ou um presente por até 300 km num dia. O cronista Martín de Murúa conta que, quando o Inca queria peixe fresco do mar, ele chegava vivo a Cusco, a 350 a 400 km do litoral, coisa que o próprio cronista achou incrível. Em 2014, a rede de estradas incas virou Patrimônio Mundial da UNESCO.

fontes.trecho: they were in charge of carrying messages in the form of quipus, oral information, or small packets. Along the Inca road system there were relay stations called chaskiwasi (house of chasqui), placed at about 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) from each other, where the chasqui switched, exchanging their message(s) with the fresh messenger. The chasqui system could deliver a message or a gift along a distance of up to 300 kilometres (190 mi) per day. [...] Quipus could represent the amount of taxes to be paid by a village or a province or the number of soldiers to be moved. There is no evidence that the chasquis could read the quipus [...] The waiting chasquis would constantly surveil the road to spot the incoming runner, the latter of which shouted within sight of the hut and played his seashell trumpet, in order to alert the new one to take his place. He gave his message, repeating it more than once, until the new chasqui understood it perfectly. [...] Murúa confirms that "When the Inca wanted to eat fresh fish from the sea, since it was seventy or eighty leagues [350 to 400 kilometres (220 to 250 mi)] (from the coast) to Cuzco, where he lived, they would bring it to him alive, which indeed seems an incredible thing [...] other chroniclers report distances of half a league or 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi).

It was about 40,000 kilometres (25,000 mi) long in total. [...] Transportation was done on foot as in pre-Columbian America; the use of wheels for transportation was not known. [...] In 2014 the road system became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. [...] The exact extent of the road network is not known: travelers and scholars proposed various lengths, spanning from 23,000 kilometres (14,000 mi) to 40,000 kilometres (25,000 mi) to 60,000 kilometres (37,000 mi).

gancho: Machu Picchu talvez não se chamasse Machu Picchu. Um estudo de 2021 sugere que o lugar era Huayna Picchu, ou só Picchu, e que o nome atual pegou com as publicações de Hiram Bingham, a partir de 1911.
explicacao: A cidadela inca fica numa sela estreita entre dois picos. Em quíchua, machu quer dizer velho, wayna quer dizer jovem e pikchu é pico: Machu Picchu é o pico velho, e Huayna Picchu, o menor ao lado. Um estudo publicado em 2021 na revista Ñawpa Pacha, do Instituto de Estudos Andinos, usou anotações de campo de Bingham, mapas antigos e documentos históricos para concluir que o nome original provavelmente era Huayna Picchu, ou apenas Picchu. No fim do século XVI, espanhóis registraram indígenas falando em voltar a "Huayna Picchu", e um atlas de 1904 marcava o lugar com esse nome. Bingham, que procurava a capital perdida do Estado neoinca, também não foi o primeiro explorador a chegar lá: o sítio era conhecido pelos moradores da região. Em 1902, o peruano Agustín Lizárraga escreveu a carvão "A. Lizárraga 1902" na janela central do Templo das Três Janelas. Em 1911, Bingham viu a inscrição e, decepcionado de início, anotou no diário de campo que Lizárraga era o descobridor de Machu Picchu. Mas foi Bingham quem levou as ruínas à fama internacional.

fontes.trecho: Although the site was known locally and reached in the early 20th century by the Peruvian explorer Agustín Lizárraga, it was brought to international attention in 1911 by the American historian Hiram Bingham III. [...] The site is on a narrow saddle between two mountain peaks, Machu Picchu and Huayna Picchu. In the Quechua language, machu means 'old' or 'old person' and wayna (spelled huayna in standard Spanish orthography) means 'young', while pikchu refers to a 'summit', 'peak', or 'pyramid'. [...] a 2021 study in Ñawpa Pacha: Journal of the Institute of Andean Studies suggests that the site was likely called "Huayna Picchu", after the smaller peak nearby, or simply "Picchu". According to the research, the association of the name Machu Picchu with the ruins likely began with American explorer Hiram Bingham's 1911 publications, a conclusion supported by Bingham's field notes, early maps, and historical documents. [...] In the late 16th century, Spaniards who had gained control of the area documented that indigenous individuals mentioned returning to "Huayna Picchu" [...] a 1904 atlas labeled it as Huayna Picchu. [...] During that visit, Lizárraga marked his surname and the year, "A. Lizárraga 1902", in charcoal on the central window of the Temple of the Three Windows. In 1911, American historian and explorer Hiram Bingham traveled the region looking for the lost capital of the Neo-Inca state [...] Bingham found the surname of Lizárraga and the 1902 date on the temple. Initially disappointed, he documented in his pocket field journal: "Agustín Lizárraga is discoverer of Machu Picchu

gancho: Do outro lado do rio Mississippi, diante da atual St. Louis, nos EUA, houve no século XII uma cidade indígena que pode ter sido maior que Londres. Seu maior monte de terra tem 30 m de altura.
explicacao: Cahokia foi o maior centro da cultura do Mississippi, que se espalhou por boa parte do centro e do sudeste dos atuais EUA a partir do ano 1000. Antes de cerca de 1050, moravam ali umas mil pessoas; depois, a cidade cresceu depressa, ao que parece com muitos imigrantes de outras regiões. No auge, cobria uns 16 km² e tinha cerca de 120 montes de terra. As estimativas de população variam muito, de 6.000 a 40.000 habitantes. Se as mais altas estiverem certas, nenhuma cidade dos EUA foi maior até a década de 1780, quando Filadélfia passou dos 40.000. A comparação com a Londres do século XII, que a própria literatura faz com um "talvez", só se sustenta pelas estimativas mais altas; pelas mais baixas, Cahokia seria menor. Para erguer montes e praças, milhares de trabalhadores moveram, ao longo de décadas, mais de 1,6 milhão de m³ de terra em cestos trançados. O maior monte, o Monks Mound, cobre 5,7 hectares, sobe 30 m e era coroado por uma grande construção que acrescentava outros 15 m de altura. O nome original da cidade é desconhecido. "Cahokia" vem de um povo indígena que vivia na área quando os primeiros exploradores franceses chegaram, no século XVII, séculos depois do abandono da cidade. Hoje o sítio é Patrimônio Mundial da UNESCO.

fontes.trecho: is the site of a Native American city which existed c. 1050 – c. 1350 AD, directly across the Mississippi River from present-day St. Louis. [...] At its apex around 1100 AD, the city covered about 6 square miles (16 km2), included about 120 earthworks [...] Cahokia was the largest and most influential urban settlement of the Mississippian culture, which developed advanced societies across much of what is now the Central and the Southeastern United States, beginning around 1000 AD. [...] The city's original name is unknown. The mounds were later named after the Cahokia tribe, a historic Illiniwek people living in the area when the first French explorers arrived in the 17th century. As this was centuries after Cahokia was abandoned by its original inhabitants [...] It is also one of the 26 UNESCO World Heritage Sites within the United States. [...] Home to about 1,000 people before circa 1050, its population grew rapidly after that date. [...] Archaeologists estimate the city's population at between 6,000 and 40,000 at its peak. If the highest population estimates are correct, Cahokia was larger than any subsequent city in the United States until the 1780s, when Philadelphia's population grew beyond 40,000. Its population in the 12th century may have been larger than that of London and Paris. Studies of Cahokia's rise see large-scale immigration as an essential contributor to the city's initial rapid growth. [...] thousands of workers over decades moved more than an estimated 55 million cubic feet (1,600,000 m3) of earth in woven baskets to create this network of mounds and community plazas. Monks Mound, for example, covers 14 acres (5.7 ha), rises 100 ft (30 m), and was topped by a massive 5,000 ft2 (460 m2) building another 50 ft (15 m) high.

gancho: Enquanto o Egito erguia as grandes pirâmides, uma cidade com pirâmides próprias prosperava no Peru: Caral. Não tinha cerâmica, e ali não apareceu sinal de guerra: nem muralhas, nem armas.
explicacao: Caral fica no vale do rio Supe, no litoral norte do Peru, e foi habitada de cerca de 2600 a 2000 a.C. É o maior sítio registrado nos Andes com datas anteriores a 2000 a.C., e seus escavadores a descrevem como o centro urbano mais antigo das Américas, título que outros pesquisadores contestam. Ela pertence à civilização de Caral-Supe, ou Norte Chico, que surgiu mil anos depois da Suméria e quase dois mil anos antes dos olmecas, na Mesoamérica. Essa sociedade não conhecia cerâmica, e dela quase não sobrou arte visual. Também não há indícios de guerra: os povoados não tinham defesas. Isso não quer dizer ausência de violência: há indícios de sacrifícios humanos rituais na região. A ausência de guerra contraria a teoria de que os primeiros Estados nasceram para defender recursos escassos. A economia ligava o litoral e o interior. Em Caral, os restos de animais são quase todos marinhos, com muita anchova e sardinha, e o algodão, principal produto da irrigação, virava redes de pesca e tecidos. Resumindo o trabalho da arqueóloga Ruth Shady, a BBC sugeriu que anchovas secas talvez servissem até como uma espécie de moeda para pagar quem trabalhava nas grandes obras.

fontes.trecho: Caral was a thriving metropolis at roughly the same time as the great pyramids were being built in Egypt [...] Caral is the largest recorded site in the Andean region, with dates older than 2000 BC. [...] Caral was inhabited from around 2600 BC to 2000 BC [...] Caral has been described by its excavators as the oldest urban center in the Americas. This claim has been challenged [...] No indications of warfare, such as battlements, weapons, or mutilated bodies, have been found at Caral. [...] There, remains of human sacrifices (two children and a newborn) have been found. [...] One such skeleton represents the earliest known evidence of human sacrifice in the Andean region, dating to around 3000 BC.

Complex society in the Caral–Supe arose a millennium after Sumer in Mesopotamia, was contemporaneous with the Egyptian pyramids, and predated the Mesoamerican Olmecs by nearly two millennia. In archaeological nomenclature, Caral–Supe is a pre-ceramic culture of the pre-Columbian Late Archaic; it completely lacked ceramics and no evidence of visual art has survived. [...] Shady notes that "animal remains are almost exclusively marine" at Caral, including clams and mussels, and large amounts of anchovies and sardines. [...] In its summation of the 2001 Shady paper, the BBC suggests workers would have been "paid or compelled" to work on centralized projects of this sort, with dried anchovies possibly serving as a form of currency. [...] Although not edible, cotton was the most important product of irrigation in the Caral–Supe culture, vital to the production of fishing nets (that in turn provided maritime resources) as well as to textiles and textile technology. [...] There is no evidence of warfare "of any kind or at any level during the Preceramic Period". Mutilated bodies, burned buildings, and other tell-tale signs of violence are absent and settlement patterns are completely non-defensive. The evidence of the development of complex government in the absence of warfare contrasts markedly to archaeological theory, which suggests that human beings move away from kin-based groups to larger units resembling "states" for mutual defense of often scarce resources.

gancho: No Peru antigo, abrir buracos no crânio era cirurgia frequente. No tempo dos incas, de 75% a 83% dos operados sobreviviam, segundo um estudo de 2018. Na Guerra Civil americana, cerca de metade morria.
explicacao: Mais de 800 crânios pré-históricos com marcas de trepanação, de um a sete buracos cada, já foram achados no litoral e nos Andes do Peru, os mais antigos de cerca de 400 a.C. São mais do que todos os crânios pré-históricos trepanados do resto do mundo somados. O neurologista David Kushner, da Universidade de Miami, e os antropólogos John Verano, de Tulane, e Anne Titelbaum compararam esse acervo com cirurgias de crânio de outras épocas. Para medir a sobrevivência, olharam a remodelação do osso em volta do buraco, sinal de cicatrização; sem ela, assumiram que o paciente morreu na cirurgia ou poucos dias depois. Por isso, os números dos Andes e os da Guerra Civil não foram medidos do mesmo jeito, e a comparação, feita pelos próprios autores, é aproximada. Entre 400 e 200 a.C., os resultados eram piores que na Guerra Civil americana, quando cerca de metade dos pacientes morria. Mas, de 1000 a 1400, a sobrevivência chegou a 91% em algumas amostras, e no período inca ficou em média entre 75% e 83%. Com o tempo, os cirurgiões andinos aprenderam quais técnicas eram mais seguras. Não se sabe o que usavam como anestesia. Segundo Verano, talvez folhas de coca, ou uma bebida fermentada, mas não há registros escritos.

fontes.titulo: Holes in the head (University of Miami News, 2018)
fontes.trecho: By Maya Bell 06-08-2018 [...] In their study published in the June issue of World Neurosurgery [...] Kushner and his co-authors—biological anthropologists John W. Verano, a world authority on Peruvian trepanation at Tulane University, and his former graduate student, Anne R. Titelbaum [...] Neither do we know what they used as anesthesia, but since there were so many (cranial surgeries) they must have used something—possibly coca leaves. Maybe there was something else, maybe a fermented beverage. There are no written records, so we just don’t know. [...] More than 800 prehistoric skulls with evidence of trepanation—at least one but as many as seven telltale holes—have been found in the coastal regions and the Andean highlands of Peru, the earliest dating back to about 400 B.C. That’s more than the combined total number of prehistoric trepanned skulls found in the rest of the world. [...] The researchers gauged survival by classifying the extent of bone remodeling around the trepanned holes, which indicates healing. If there was no evidence of healing the researchers assumed th [...] The long-term survival rates from such “shallow surgeries” in Peru during those early years, from about 400 to 200 B.C., proved to be worse than those in the Civil War, when about half the patients died. But, from 1000 to 1400 A.D., survival rates improved dramatically, to as high as 91 percent in some samples, to an average of 75 to 83 percent during the Incan period, the study showed. “Over time, from the earliest to the latest, they learned which techniques were better

gancho: Os vikings cortaram árvores na Terra Nova, no Canadá, no ano de 1021, séculos antes de Colombo. A data exata saiu de uma marca deixada nos anéis das árvores por um pico de radiação cósmica no ano 993.
explicacao: L'Anse aux Meadows, na ponta norte da ilha de Terra Nova, é o único sítio indiscutível de contato transoceânico de europeus com as Américas antes de Colombo, fora a Groenlândia. Faltava saber quando os nórdicos estiveram lá: as datas por radiocarbono iam de 990 a 1050. A pista veio do céu. No ano 993, um evento de radiação cósmica fez subir de repente a produção de carbono radioativo na atmosfera, e o salto ficou gravado, ao mesmo tempo, nos anéis de árvores do mundo todo. Os pesquisadores acharam esse salto em três peças de madeira do sítio, cortadas com ferramentas de metal, que os povos indígenas da região não fabricavam na época. Como as peças conservavam a borda logo abaixo da casca, deu para contar os anéis até o último e chegar ao ano exato em que as árvores foram derrubadas. As três, de árvores diferentes, deram o mesmo ano, 1021, coincidência que os autores do estudo, publicado na Nature em 2021, chamaram de notável e inesperada. É a única data segura de presença europeia do outro lado do Atlântico antes das viagens de Colombo. Para os autores, ela marca também o primeiro momento conhecido em que os seres humanos fecharam a volta ao globo.

fontes.titulo: Evidence for European presence in the Americas in AD 1021 (Nature)
fontes.trecho: Published: 20 October 2021 [...] Transatlantic exploration took place centuries before the crossing of Columbus. [...] Here we provide evidence that the Vikings were present in Newfoundland in ad 1021. We overcome the imprecision of previous age estimates by making use of the cosmic-ray-induced upsurge in atmospheric radiocarbon concentrations in ad 993 (ref. 6). Our new date lays down a marker for European cognisance of the Americas, and represents the first known point at which humans encircled the globe. [...] However, such time series have also revealed that production of the isotope rapidly increased in the years ad; 775 and ad 993 [...] These sudden increases were caused by cosmic radiation events, and appear synchronously in dendrochronological records all around the world [...] if the bark edge (or more specifically, the waney edge) is also present, it becomes possible to determine the exact felling year of the tree [...] they had all been modified by metal tools, evident from their characteristically clean, low angle-in cuts30. Such implements were not manufactured by the Indigenous inhabitants of the area at the time [...] Our result of ad 1021 for the cutting year constitutes the only secure calendar date for the presence of Europeans across the Atlantic before the voyages of Columbus. Moreover, the fact that our results, on three different trees, converge on the same year is notable and unexpected.

With carbon dating estimates between 990 and 1050 CE (mean date 1014) and tree-ring dating of 1021, L'Anse aux Meadows is the only undisputed site of pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact of Europeans with the Americas outside of Greenland.

gancho: Entre as múmias feitas de propósito mais antigas do mundo estão as do povo chinchorro, no deserto do Atacama, no Chile, desde cerca de 5050 a.C. E não só da elite: crianças também.
explicacao: Os chinchorros eram caçadores-coletores marinhos que viviam no litoral do norte do Chile e do sul do Peru. O Atacama, hiperárido e com solo rico em nitratos, já conservava corpos sozinho: o mais antigo conhecido desse povo, o Homem de Acha, morreu por volta de 7020 a.C. Por volta de 5050 a.C., eles passaram a mumificar os mortos de propósito, e o exemplo mais antigo é uma criança enterrada no vale de Camarones. Por décadas, foram tidas como as múmias artificiais mais antigas do mundo. Em 2025, um estudo na PNAS, de arqueólogos da Universidade Nacional da Austrália, propôs que corpos secos lentamente na fumaça de fogueiras no sul da China e no Sudeste Asiático, entre 12 mil e 4 mil anos atrás, teriam exemplares ainda mais antigos. Segundo a UNESCO, desmontavam e remontavam sistematicamente os corpos de homens, mulheres e crianças de toda a escala social. Os métodos incluíam reforçar os corpos e modelá-los com argila, e os arqueólogos reconhecem vários estilos, como as múmias negras, as vermelhas, as cobertas de barro e as enfaixadas. A prática durou cerca de 3.000 anos e acabou por volta de 1800 a.C. Hoje, as múmias enfrentam um inimigo vivo. No acervo da Universidade de Tarapacá, em Arica, a pele de algumas escureceu e começou a verter líquido. Pesquisadores acharam ali bactérias e fungos capazes de quebrar colágeno e queratina, e o estrago acelera muito com umidade relativa de 75% a 80%.

fontes.trecho: The oldest known naturally preserved Chinchorro individual dates to about 7020 BCE, while deliberate mummification began by about 5050 BCE, making the Chinchorro mummies the oldest known examples of purposefully preserved human bodies in the world. The Chinchorro artificially preserved men, women and children from across their communities rather than restricting elaborate funerary treatment to a social elite. Their methods included reconstructing and reinforcing bodies, modelling them with clay [...] In 2021, settlements and cemeteries associated with the Chinchorro culture and its tradition of artificial mummification in Chile's Arica and Parinacota Region were designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. [...] known as Acha Man, died around 7020 BCE. His body was preserved by the hyper-arid conditions of the Atacama Desert. By about 5050 BCE, the Chinchorro had begun preserving their dead through artificial mummification. The earliest known example is a child buried in the Camarones Valley [...] Artificial mummification continued for about 3,000 years before ending around 1800 BCE. Archaeologists recognise several forms of Chinchorro mummification, including black, red, mud-coated and bandage mummies. [...] the previous decade among mummies held at the University of Tarapacá in Arica, northern Chile. Areas of preserved skin had darkened and begun to ooze. Researchers from Harvard University and the University of Tarapacá found bacteria and fungi on the damaged skin, including microorganisms capable of breaking down collagen and keratin, important proteins in human skin. Experiments showed that deterioration increased sharply at 75–80 percent relative humidity. [...] The soil is very rich in nitrates which, when combined with other factors such as the aridity of the Atacama Desert, ensure organic preservation.

fontes.titulo: Settlement and Artificial Mummification of the Chinchorro Culture in the Arica and Parinacota Region (UNESCO World Heritage)
fontes.trecho: they bear testimony to a culture of marine hunter-gatherers who resided in the arid and hostile northern coast of the Atacama Desert [...] Over time, the Chinchorro perfected complex mortuary practices, whereby they systematically dismembered and reassembled bodies of deceased men, women and children of the entire social spectrum to create “artificial” mummies.

fontes.titulo: World’s oldest mummies found in Asia (Revista Pesquisa FAPESP, 2025)
fontes.trecho: World’s oldest mummies found in Asia [...] HUNG, H.-C. et al. PNAS. 2025 [...] After examining the remains of 54 human bodies, archaeologists from the Australian National University identified human mummies in Southeast Asia [...] Between 12,000 and 4,000 years ago, hunter-gatherers in southern China, Southeast Asia, and nearby islands—including Borneo and Java—bound their dead in squatting positions and slowly dried them over smoldering, low-temperature fires for several months before burial. Lengthy exposure to smoke mummified the skin of the corpses

gancho: Nos Andes, batata é liofilizada sem máquina há séculos: congela nas noites do Altiplano, seca ao sol e é pisoteada pela família. Leve e durável, o chuño era comida de soldado inca em marcha.
explicacao: O chuño é feito por comunidades quíchuas e aimarás da Bolívia e do Peru com uma variedade de batata amarga e resistente à geada. Em junho e julho, acima de 3.800 m de altitude, as noites chegam a uns −5 °C. As batatinhas são espalhadas bem juntas no chão, congelam à noite e perdem água de dia, por cerca de três noites: é uma liofilização natural. O congelamento rompe as paredes das células, o que facilita tirar a água que resta. Aí entra a família inteira, que faz montinhos de batata e "dança" em cima deles, espremendo a água e soltando as cascas. Lavado por cerca de uma semana e seco ao sol, vira o chuño branco; sem a lavagem, o chuño negro. A técnica é anterior ao Império Inca: há chuño em sítios arqueológicos de Tiwanaku, perto do lago Titicaca. Por ser portátil, durar muito e alimentar bem, era levado pelos soldados incas em marcha. Carl Troll chegou a defender que as noites abaixo de zero que permitem fazer chuño favoreceram a ascensão do império. A palavra vem do quíchua ch'uñu, "batata congelada".

fontes.trecho: is a preserved potato product traditionally made by Quechua and Aymara communities of Bolivia and Peru [...] obtained by exposing a bitter, frost-resistant variety of potatoes to the very low night temperatures of the Andean Altiplano, freezing them, and subsequently exposing them to the intense sunlight of the day [...] The word comes from Quechua ch'uñu, meaning 'frozen potato' [...] The existence of chuño dates back to before the time of the Inca Empire in the 13th century, based on findings that have been made of the product at various archaeological sites. Specifically, they have been found at Tiwanaku [...] Due to its portability, long shelf life, and nutritional value, chuño was eaten by Inca soldiers on marches. Indeed Carl Troll argued that the nighttime sub-freezing temperatures of southern Peruvian highlands that allowed for chuño production favoured the rise of the Inca Empire. [...] Chuño is made at the beginning of winter during June and July, during which time the temperatures reach around −5 °C (23 °F) at elevations of over 3,800 metres (12,500 ft). [...] These small potatoes are spread closely on flat ground, and allowed to freeze with the low night temperatures and dehydrate in the daytime, for about three nights. This process results in natural freeze-drying. [...] During the process of manually squeezing water out of the potatoes via stepping on them, whole families will participate. The previous freeze-drying breaks down cell walls, making it easier to remove water from the potatoes. They build a small pile of potatoes with their feet and then "dance" on the pile, removing the skins as they do so. [...] This washing typically takes about a week. The final step is drying in the sun. [...] Black chuño is obtained directly from the original freezing, trampling, and refreezing process. The product is not washed or exposed to water again
is most commonly associated with the Tiwanaku culture of the Lake Titicaca region

gancho: Levou quase um século para achar 430 figuras desenhadas no deserto de Nazca, no Peru. Com a ajuda de inteligência artificial, uma equipe achou mais 303 em só seis meses de campo, quase dobrando a conta.
explicacao: Além das famosas figuras gigantes, o deserto de Nazca guarda geoglifos menores, em relevo, muito difíceis de enxergar. Pesquisadores do Instituto Nazca da Universidade de Yamagata, no Japão, com a IBM Research, usaram um sistema de inteligência artificial para varrer imagens de toda a região e apontar candidatos. Só a triagem das fotos indicadas pela IA tomou 1.200 horas de trabalho, e a checagem a pé, entre setembro de 2022 e fevereiro de 2023, mais 1.440 horas. O resultado, publicado em 2024, foram 303 figuras novas confirmadas, entre elas papagaios, gatos, macacos, orcas e cabeças decepadas. Com o acervo maior, deu para comparar os dois tipos. As figuras gigantes de linha retratam sobretudo animais selvagens (64%) e ficam, em média, a 34 m da rede de linhas e trapézios usada em cerimônias. Já 81,6% das figuras em relevo mostram humanos ou coisas modificadas por humanos, como camelídeos domesticados e cabeças decepadas, e ficam em média a 43 m de antigas trilhas que cruzam o deserto. Para os autores, as grandes provavelmente serviam a rituais da comunidade, e as pequenas eram feitas e vistas por indivíduos ou pequenos grupos de passagem.

fontes.titulo: AI-accelerated Nazca survey nearly doubles the number of known figurative geoglyphs and sheds light on their purpose (PNAS, 2024)
fontes.trecho: It took nearly a century to discover a total of 430 figurative Nazca geoglyphs, which offer significant insights into the ancient cultures at the Nazca Pampa. Here, we report the deployment of an AI system to the entire Nazca region, a UNESCO World Heritage site, leading to the discovery of 303 new figurative geoglyphs within only 6 mo of field survey, nearly doubling the number of known figurative geoglyphs. Even with limited training examples, the developed AI approach is demonstrated to be effective in detecting the smaller relief-type geoglyphs, which unlike the giant line-type geoglyphs are very difficult to discern. [...] We find that relief-type geoglyphs depict mainly human motifs or motifs of things modified by humans, such as domesticated animals and decapitated heads (81.6%). They are typically located within viewing distance (on average 43 m) of ancient trails that crisscross the Nazca Pampa and were most likely built and viewed at the individual or small-group level. On the other hand, the giant line-type figurative geoglyphs mainly depict wild animals (64%). They are found an average of 34 m from the elaborate linear/trapezoidal network of geoglyphs, which suggests that they were probably built and used on a community level for ritual activities.

In 2024, a team of archaeologists from the Yamagata University's Nazca Institute, in collaboration with IBM Research, used artificial intelligence (AI) to discover 303 previously unknown geoglyphs depicting parrots, cats, monkeys, killer whales, and even severed heads near the Nazca Lines in Peru. The field survey took place between September 2022 and February 2023 and was conducted on foot for ground truthing [...] It required 1,440 labor hours and resulted in 303 newly confirmed figurative geoglyphs. [...] A total of 1,200 labor hours were spent screening the AI-model geoglyph candidate photos.

gancho: Murais pintados há mais de mil anos no México mantêm um azul vivo num dos climas mais duros do mundo. O segredo do azul maia é juntar anil com uma argila, o que o torna resistente até a ácido nítrico.
explicacao: O azul maia, um turquesa intenso, foi fabricado por povos da Mesoamérica, como maias e astecas. Foi usado em murais, cerâmicas, esculturas e códices. Murais de Chichén Itzá, Bonampak e Cacaxtla conservam a cor há mais de mil anos. O pigmento junta duas partes: o corante índigo, tirado das folhas do anil, e a paligorsquita, uma argila natural. A combinação é extremamente estável: resiste a solventes, ácidos, álcalis e à biodegradação, e só se desfaz com um tratamento ácido muito intenso. A composição foi desvendada no século XX, com análises de difração. Depois da conquista, o azul ainda foi usado no século XVI em conventos do México colonial, mas depois a técnica se perdeu no México. Em 1993, o historiador e químico mexicano Constantino Reyes-Valerio publicou uma receita que reconstitui o processo antigo, juntando a leitura de crônicas antigas com análises microscópicas e espectroscopia das pinturas. Hoje o pigmento inspira químicos a criar cores novas, como o "violeta maia".

fontes.trecho: is a unique bright turquoise or azure blue pigment manufactured by cultures of pre-Columbian Mesoamerica, such as the Mayas and Aztecs [...] It is found in mural paintings on architectural buildings, ceramic pieces, sculptures, codices [...] Murals painted more than 1,000 years ago in Chichén Itzá, Bonampak and Cacaxtla, in what is today Mexico, have maintained their color, despite existing in one of the world's harshest climates. [...] primarily indigo dyes derived from the leaves of anil (Indigofera suffruticosa, called ch'oj in Mayan) plants combined with palygorskite, a natural clay [...] Maya blue first appeared around 800, and it was still used in the 16th century in several Convents of Colonial Mexico [...] After that, the techniques for its production were lost in Mexico [...] The color has resisted chemical solvents and acids such as nitric acid. Its resistance against chemical aggression (acids, alkalis, solvents, etc.) and biodegradation was tested, and it was shown that Maya blue is an extremely resistant pigment, but it can be destroyed using very intense acid treatment under reflux. Because of its exceptionally durable colour properties, Maya Blue is an iconic system that led to paleo-inspired chemistry, i.e. the recreation of new pigments such as Maya Violet [...] The chemical composition of the compound was determined by powder diffraction in the 1950s [...] An actual recipe to reproduce Maya blue pigment was published in 1993 by a Mexican historian and chemist, Constantino Reyes-Valerio. [...] through a thorough revision of primary texts (Sahagún, Hernandez, Jimenez, and others), microscopic analysis of the mural paintings and fourier transform infrared spectroscopy.

gancho: No Peru, uma ponte de capim trançado sobre o rio Apurímac é refeita todo ano por quatro comunidades quíchuas, com técnicas incas. É a última ponte de corda inca que resta.
explicacao: A Q'eswachaka é uma ponte suspensa sobre um desfiladeiro do rio Apurímac, no sul dos Andes. A renovação dura só três dias, na segunda semana de junho, mas organiza o ano inteiro das comunidades de Huinchiri, Chaupibanda, Choccayhua e Ccollana Quehue. Primeiro, as famílias cortam e torcem capim para fazer cordas finas de uns 70 m. Dois mestres construtores guiam a torção dessas cordas em cordas médias, que depois são trançadas em seis cabos grossos. Os homens amarram os cabos a bases de pedra antigas, e os artesãos tecem a ponte, cada um partindo de uma margem. No tempo dos incas, o trabalho teria sido uma forma de imposto, a mit'a. Hoje existe uma ponte moderna ali perto, mas os construtores dizem que mantêm a tradição para honrar os antepassados e a Pachamama, a Mãe Terra. Em 2013, a UNESCO pôs os saberes e rituais da renovação na lista do patrimônio cultural imaterial da humanidade. Sem manutenção na pandemia de covid-19, a ponte desabou em março de 2021 e foi reconstruída nas semanas seguintes.

fontes.titulo: Knowledge, skills and rituals related to the annual renewal of the Q’eswachaka bridge (UNESCO)
fontes.trecho: Inscribed in 2013 (8.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity [...] The Q’eswachaka bridge is a rope suspension bridge over a gorge of the Apurimac River in the southern Andes. It is renewed every year, using traditional Inca techniques and raw materials. The Quechua-speaking peasant communities of Huinchiri, Chaupibanda, Choccayhua and Ccollana Quehue [...] Although the renewal lasts only three days, it structures the life of the participating communities all year round [...] The process begins with families cutting and twisting straw to form thin ropes about 70 m long. Two bridge-builders then guide the process of twisting them together to form medium-sized ropes, which are then braided to form six great ropes. When these are ready, men from the community tie the ropes tightly to ancient stone bases. The craftspeople then lead the weaving of the bridge, each starting from opposite ends.

is the last remaining Inca rope bridge, consisting of grass ropes that span the Apurímac River [...] Even though there is a modern bridge nearby, the residents of the region keep the ancient tradition and skills alive by renewing the bridge annually, during the second week of June. [...] In ancient times the effort would have been a form of tax (Mit'a), with participants expected to perform the rebuilding; nowadays the builders have indicated that the effort is performed to honor their ancestors and the Pachamama (Earth Mother). [...] Due to a lack of maintenance during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and early 2021, the bridge collapsed in March 2021. In the following weeks the bridge was rebuilt.

gancho: Teotihuacan, a maior cidade das Américas no seu auge, foi batizada pelos astecas séculos depois de cair, como "lugar onde nasceram os deuses". Seu nome original é desconhecido, e quem a governava também.
explicacao: Teotihuacan fica a 40 km da Cidade do México e é famosa pelas pirâmides do Sol e da Lua. Apesar da proximidade, não era asteca: é séculos mais antiga que o império deles. No auge, talvez na primeira metade do primeiro milênio, foi a maior cidade das Américas, provavelmente com cerca de 100.000 moradores, e tudo indica que reunia vários povos. Por volta de 550, seus monumentos foram saqueados e queimados. Os astecas, falantes de náuatle, deram ao lugar o nome Teōtīhuacān, traduzido como "lugar onde nasceram os deuses", porque acreditavam que os deuses tinham criado o universo ali. O nome original é desconhecido; em textos hieroglíficos maias, a cidade aparece como puh, "lugar dos juncos". O poder também intriga. Cidades maias e zapotecas da época, e antes delas os olmecas, deixaram palácios reais e cenas de guerra, conquista e cativos humilhados, marcas de dinastias autoritárias. Em Teotihuacan, nada disso foi achado, e muitos estudiosos concluem que ela tinha alguma forma de governo coletivo. Mesmo assim, sua influência ia longe: em 378, um chefe guerreiro retratado com símbolos de Teotihuacan conquistou Tikal, a 1.000 km dali, e trocou o rei maia.

fontes.trecho: is located in the State of Mexico, 40 kilometers (25 mi) northeast of modern-day Mexico City. Teotihuacan is known today as the site of many of the most architecturally significant Mesoamerican pyramids built in the pre-Columbian Americas, namely the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon. Although close to Mexico City, Teotihuacan was not a Mexica (i.e. Aztec) city, and it predates the Aztec Empire by many centuries. At its zenith, perhaps in the first half of the first millennium (1 CE to 500 CE), Teotihuacan was the largest city in the Americas. Its population has been estimated to be at least 25,000, but likely sat around 100,000 during its height [...] Its major monuments were sacked and systematically burned around 550 CE. [...] The name Teōtīhuacān was given by the Nahuatl-speaking Aztecs centuries after the fall of the city around 550 CE. The term has been glossed as "birthplace of the gods", or "place where gods were born" [...] This is because the Aztecs believed that the gods created the universe at that site. [...] The original name of the city is unknown, but it appears in hieroglyphic texts from the Maya region as puh, or "Place of Reeds". [...] Contemporaneous cities in the same region, including Mayan and Zapotec, as well as the earlier Olmec civilization, left ample attestations of dynastic authoritarian sovereignty in the form of royal palaces, ceremonial ball courts, and depictions of war, conquest, and humiliated captives. However, no such artifacts have been found in Teotihuacan. Many scholars have thus concluded that Teotihuacan was led by some sort of "collective governance." In January 378, the warlord Sihyaj K'ahk' [...] depicted with artifacts and the feather-serpent imagery associated with Teotihuacan culture, conquered Tikal, 1,000 kilometres (600 mi) away from Teotihuacan, removing and replacing the Maya king [...] Archeological evidence suggests that Teotihuacan was a multi-ethnic city

gancho: Os astecas não se chamavam de astecas: eram os mexicas. Num relato da migração deles, o próprio deus Huitzilopochtli avisa que o nome do povo não é mais Azteca. O termo foi popularizado por Humboldt, em 1810.
explicacao: Em náuatle, aztēcatl quer dizer "gente de Aztlán", um lugar de origem mítico reivindicado por vários povos do centro do México. A palavra aparece nos relatos de migração dos mexicas para descrever as tribos que saíram juntas de Aztlán, mas não era o nome que eles usavam para si. Num desses relatos, Huitzilopochtli, o deus protetor dos mexicas, diz aos seguidores, no meio da jornada, que eles já não se chamam Azteca, e sim Mexitin, ou seja, mexicas. Os moradores de Tenochtitlan, cidade numa ilha do lago Texcoco, onde hoje fica a Cidade do México, chamavam a si mesmos de Mēxihcah. Foi o cientista alemão Alexander von Humboldt quem, em 1810, popularizou "asteca" como nome coletivo para todos os povos ligados ao Estado mexica e à Tríplice Aliança por comércio, costumes, religião e língua. Essa aliança, que chamamos de Império Asteca, era uma confederação de três cidades-Estado formada em 1427: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco e Tlacopan. Hoje o termo "asteca" ora se refere só aos mexicas de Tenochtitlan, ora a vários povos de língua náuatle do centro do México.

fontes.trecho: The Aztec Empire was a confederation of three city-states established in 1427: Tenochtitlan (the capital of Mexica), Tetzcoco, and Tlacopan. Although the term Aztecs is often narrowly restricted to the Mexica of Tenochtitlan, it is also broadly used to refer to Nahua polities or peoples of central Mexico in the pre-Hispanic era [...] mean "people from Aztlán", a mythical place of origin for several ethnic groups in central Mexico. The term was not used as an endonym by the Aztecs themselves, but it is found in the different migration accounts of the Mexica, where it describes the different tribes who left Aztlan together. In one account of the journey from Aztlan, Huitzilopochtli, the tutelary deity of the Mexica tribe, tells his followers on the journey that "now, no longer is your name Azteca, you are now Mexitin [Mexica]". In today's usage, the term "Aztec" often refers exclusively to the Mexica people of Tenochtitlan (now the location of Mexico City), situated on an island in Lake Texcoco, who referred to themselves as Mēxihcah [...] Alexander von Humboldt originated the modern usage of "Aztec" in 1810, as a collective term applied to all the people linked by trade, custom, religion, and language to the Mexica state and the Triple Alliance. [...] German scientist Alexander von Humboldt

gancho: Os "jardins flutuantes" dos astecas não flutuavam: eram ilhas artificiais erguidas no fundo raso do lago, cercadas por varas e juncos. Com água ao redor o ano todo, podiam dar até sete colheitas por ano.
explicacao: As chinampas eram canteiros retangulares construídos em lagos e pântanos de água doce do vale do México. Os agricultores fincavam estacas no leito raso e cercavam o retângulo com um trançado de varas; lá dentro, o acúmulo de terra e de plantas aquáticas formava a ilha. Canais largos o bastante para uma canoa separavam um canteiro do outro. Com água por perto o tempo todo, as plantas não dependiam da chuva, e a produtividade era altíssima: segundo algumas estimativas, até sete colheitas por ano. Os astecas não inventaram a técnica, mas foram os primeiros a usá-la em grande escala, e as chinampas cercavam Tenochtitlan, a capital. Ali, os canteiros mediam de 90 m × 5 m a 90 m × 10 m. A ideia tem parentes nos Andes: perto do lago Titicaca, os waru waru alternavam canteiros elevados e canais, e a terra elevada protegia as plantações da geada noturna. As chinampas que restam, como as de Xochimilco, foram reconhecidas pela ONU, em 2018, como Sistema Importante do Patrimônio Agrícola Mundial. Mas sofrem com a expansão urbana, a falta de água e a poluição por esgoto não tratado.

fontes.trecho: They are built up on wetlands of a lake or freshwater swamp for agricultural purposes [...] This method was also used and occupied most of Lake Xochimilco. The United Nations designated it a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System in 2018. [...] The Aztecs did not invent the chinampa technology but rather were the first to develop it to a large-scale cultivation. Sometimes called "floating gardens," chinampas did not float but are artificial islands that were created by interweaving reeds with stakes beneath the lake's surface, creating underwater fences. [...] making crops grown there independent of rainfall. Chinampas were separated by channels wide enough for a canoe to pass. These raised, well-watered beds had very high crop yields with up to 7 harvests a year. [...] In Tenochtitlan, the chinampas ranged from 90 m × 5 m (300 ft × 20 ft) to 90 m × 10 m (300 ft × 30 ft) They were created by staking out the shallow lake bed and then fencing in the rectangle with wattle. [...] Chinampa farms also ringed Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital [...] Other challenges include limited water supply, the use of pesticides, climate change, urban sprawl, and water pollution caused by untreated sewage and toxic waste.

This type of altiplano field agriculture consists of parallel canals alternated by raised planting beds [...] By trapping solar radiation during the day, this raised field agricultural method also protected crops from freezing overnight. [...] is most commonly associated with the Tiwanaku culture of the Lake Titicaca region

gancho: A Peste Negra matou de 30% a 40% dos britânicos e deixou faltar mão de obra. Em 1351, o Parlamento inglês reagiu com uma lei que tabelava salários no nível de antes da peste e prendia quem recusasse trabalho.
explicacao: Com tanta gente morta, quem sobrou para trabalhar a terra ganhou poder de barganha e passou a exigir pagamentos maiores, o que também alimentou a inflação. A elite reclamou da mudança. Primeiro veio uma ordenança do rei Eduardo III, em 1349, e depois o Estatuto dos Trabalhadores, de 1351, aprovado pelo Parlamento. O texto da lei registra a queixa: os servos se recusavam a servir a não ser por pagamentos duas ou três vezes maiores que os de antes. A resposta foi um teto: os salários deviam voltar aos valores de 1346, com preços fixados para lavradores, pastores, ceifeiros e debulhadores. Quem tivesse corpo capaz e nada de que viver era obrigado a servir a quem o chamasse, sob pena de prisão. A lei também limitava o deslocamento em busca de condições melhores. A versão mais difundida diz que ela foi mal aplicada e não impediu a alta dos salários reais, mas há um porém: logo depois da peste, os salários reais não subiram, apesar da falta de braços. O estatuto foi uma das causas, entre outras, da Revolta dos Camponeses de 1381.

fontes.trecho: The Statute of Labourers (25 Edw. 3. Stat. 2) was an act of the Parliament of England under King Edward III in 1351 in response to a labour shortage, which aimed at regulating the labour force by prohibiting requesting or offering a wage higher than pre-Plague standards and limiting movement in search of better conditions. The popular narrative about its success and enforcement holds that it was poorly enforced and did not stop the rise in real wages. However, immediately after the Black Death, real wages did not rise, despite the labour shortage. [...] The Black Death, a pandemic of bubonic plague, killed more than one-third of the population of Europe and 30–40% of the population in Britain and caused a dramatic decrease in the supply of labour. [...] Labourers had increased bargaining power and commanded higher wages. The increase in labour cost also led to inflation throughout the economy. The elite class lamented the sudden shift in economic power. In an attempt to control labour costs and price levels, Edward III issued the Ordinance of Labourers 1349 (23 Edw. 3). Parliament attempted to reinforce the Ordinance with the Statute of Labourers. It was one of the causes, among others, of the Peasants' Revolt in 1381. [...] The statute set a maximum wage for labourers that was commensurate with wages paid before the Black Death, specifically, in the year 1346. [...] That every person, able in body [...] not having enough to live upon, being required, shall be bound to serve him that doth require him, or else be committed to gaol [...] unless they have livery and wages double or treble of what they were wont to take in the twentieth year and earlier [...] Item that carters, ploughmen, drivers of ploughs, shepherds, swineherds, day men, and all other servants shall take the liveries and wages accustomed in the twentieth year [...] and reapers of corn in the first week of August 2 d [...] Item that none take for the threshing of a quarter of wheat or rye over 2½ d

gancho: Em 536, o Sol brilhou fraco e azulado por meses, e o verão europeu esfriou até 2,5 °C. Eram erupções vulcânicas. Um historiador chamou o ano de começo de um dos piores períodos para se estar vivo, se não o pior ano.
explicacao: No começo de 536, ou talvez no fim de 535, uma erupção lançou na atmosfera uma grande quantidade de aerossóis de sulfato, que barraram parte da luz do Sol. Hoje se sabe que houve pelo menos três erupções, e de onde vieram ainda é incerto. Em março de 536, Constantinopla já via o céu escurecido. O historiador Procópio escreveu que o Sol dava luz sem brilho, como num eclipse. O estadista romano Cassiodoro descreveu raios fracos e azulados, sombras que sumiam ao meio-dia e geadas na colheita que endureciam maçãs e azedavam uvas. Anais irlandeses registraram falta de pão, e textos chineses falam de grande frio, fome e neve em agosto. Anéis de carvalhos irlandeses mostram crescimento anormalmente baixo em 536. Uma nova erupção, em 539–540, esfriou o verão europeu em até 2,7 °C. As erupções provocaram quebras de safra, e a época também teve fome, a Peste de Justiniano e milhões de mortes; começou ali um período frio que durou de 536 a 660. A frase sobre o pior ano é do historiador Michael McCormick.

fontes.trecho: The volcanic winter was caused by at least three eruptions of uncertain origin, with several possible locations proposed in various continents. In early AD 536 (or possibly late 535), an eruption ejected great amounts of sulfate aerosols into the atmosphere, reducing the solar radiation reaching the Earth's surface and cooling the atmosphere for several years. In March 536, Constantinople began experiencing darkened skies and lower temperatures. Summer temperatures in 536 fell by as much as 2.5 °C (4.5 °F) below European normal. The lingering effect of the volcanic winter of 536 was augmented in the years 539 and 540, when another volcanic eruption caused summer temperatures to decline as much as 2.7 °C (4.9 °F) below European normal. [...] The volcanic eruptions caused crop failures, and were accompanied by the Plague of Justinian, famine, and millions of deaths and initiated the Late Antique Little Ice Age, which lasted from 536 to 660. Historian Michael McCormick has called the year 536 "the beginning of one of the worst periods to be alive, if not the worst year." [...] For the sun gave forth its light without brightness... and it seemed exceedingly like the sun in eclipse [...] The sun's rays were weak, and they appeared a "bluish" colour. At noon, no shadows from people were visible on the ground. [...] Frosts during harvest, which made apples harden and grapes sour. [...] "A failure of bread in AD 536" – the Annals of Ulster [...] The Bei Shi (北史; History of the North), which mentions the "great cold" and "famine" that occurred in autumn 536. [...] Low temperatures, even snow during the summer (snow reportedly fell in August in China, which caused the harvest there to be delayed). [...] shows abnormally little growth in Irish oak in 536

gancho: Na França, um castelo é construído desde 1997 só com ferramentas, materiais e técnicas do século XIII. Técnicas reaprendidas nessa obra ajudaram na reconstrução da Notre-Dame de Paris após o incêndio de 2019.
explicacao: O castelo de Guédelon fica numa floresta perto de Treigny, a duas horas ao sul de Paris. É um projeto de arqueologia experimental: para entender a tecnologia da Idade Média, a obra usa só técnicas, ferramentas e até roupas da época, e a madeira e a pedra vêm do próprio local. O terreno, uma antiga pedreira de arenito no meio da mata, com um lago perto, foi escolhido justamente porque transportar materiais era caro na Idade Média. O projeto segue o modelo de castelo desenvolvido nos séculos XII e XIII sob o rei Filipe II da França. A obra começou sob o comando do empresário Michel Guyot, que restaurava as ruínas de outro castelo, o de Saint-Fargeau, a 13 km dali. A primeira pedra foi posta em 20 de junho de 1997. Em 1998, a muralha já tinha um metro de altura, e em 2010 a torre principal chegava a 15 metros. Entre as técnicas recuperadas estão os guindastes movidos por gente caminhando dentro de uma grande roda. Técnicas redesenvolvidas em Guédelon foram aproveitadas na reconstrução da Notre-Dame de Paris, depois do incêndio de 2019. Em 2014, o canteiro recebia cerca de 300 mil visitantes por ano e foi chamado de maior experimento arqueológico do mundo.

fontes.trecho: Guédelon Castle (French: Château de Guédelon [ʃɑto d(ə) ɡedlɔ̃]) is a castle under construction near Treigny, France. The castle is the focus of an experimental archaeology project aimed at recreating a 13th-century castle and its environment using period techniques, dress, and materials. In order to fully investigate the technology required in the medieval past, the project is using only period construction techniques, tools, and costumes. Materials, including wood and stone, are all obtained locally. Jacques Moulin, chief architect for the project, designed the castle according to the architectural model developed during the 12th and 13th centuries by Philip II of France.
